tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-06 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Overweight, carried; the condition for Double Overweight (defensives leading for a second month with the industry's relative strength at B or better) is half met: defensives lead on all five windows, the three-month line at +6.6 points, but Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: C now, D prior, short of B. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Three live holdings (Carlsberg 4.67%, Fevertree 2.48%, Hilton Food 4.78%, 11.93 points) read A on Thematic Fit/Momentum through this row. Counter-case: a defensive destination two months into a rotation is crowded, and no staples house view was read this week. To A if relative strength reaches B with defensives still leading at three months.

sector.why: Overweight, carried, with a China warning named. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): staples are the rotation's destination, but AB InBev's Asia-Pacific volumes fell 11% on Chinese beer demand (Outset Global, 29 October), and China is the weak sector within staples. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, D prior, the market has started to pay. Two live holdings, Carlsberg (3.98%, with China exposure, Sell-side Momentum D) and Fevertree (2.00%), judged in component 4. Counter-case: the China leg is a company-level read on one brewer. Holds B with the staples industry; moves to A with it if defensives lead for a second month and the China read does not spread.

geography.why: Underweight, carried unchanged with the reason strengthened. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the spillover from France to Italy is the new fact this week (Goldman, 16 Oct, 'tentative spillover to Italy'), and the Italian listings in the Pool are bank-heavy (Monte dei Paschi, Credito Emiliano, Mediobanca) beside global businesses (Eni, Saipem, Tenaris, STMicroelectronics, Technoprobe, Reply). Not Double Underweight because Goldman also says contagion risk is lower than in 2011-15, its fragmentation index shows risk 'remains limited', and Southern European banks are healthier; relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to F if the fragmentation index rises or the Italian premium is read above 150 basis points; back to C under 100.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
